title: Edgewood Residences: a park-side oasis in a dense corner of Setapak.
excerpt: The open-market sister of the Sky Awani affordable series, beside a central park and new commercial hub in the SkySanctuary master plan. Sean loves the design and placemaking, but warns of the dense surroundings.
takeaways: A 1,047 sq ft three-bedroom lists at about RM580,000 to RM590,000 and asks about RM3,000 in rent.
Wide 1.9 m corridors, an open-air lobby and a gate straight into the township's central park.
The approach roads are lined with PPR flats and illegal parking, and nearby land will be developed.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Edgewood is the developer's open-market project within its SkySanctuary master plan, which also includes the Sky Awani affordable series, a temporary commercial hub with eateries, a gym and a mart, a lake and a central park. The car park facade is dressed with planter boxes, the lobby is open-air, corridors are 1.9 m wide, and a floor at car-park level has a kindergarten, a gourmet kitchen and a gate straight into the park. The deck has an infinity pool, a jacuzzi under a glass pitched-roof pavilion and a gym overlooking the park.

Sean viewed the 1,047 sq ft three-bedroom, two-bathroom Type B: living and dining side by side for 5.8 m along a balcony, a 4 m-wide front room, a kitchen with a yard that can serve as a wet kitchen, spare tiles for repairs, a large master bedroom and safe, enclosed ledges for air-conditioner installers.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: SkySanctuary sits off Jalan Genting Klang in Setapak, reached past PPR flats and old village houses, with its own guardhouse at the entrance to the zone. A new road links to DUKE and Jalan Semarak, about 15 minutes from KLCC, and an MRT3 station is planned nearby. Schools, places of worship and community centres are close, and the developer's SkyBlox rents furnished rooms nearby for about RM630 a month.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Listings ask about RM580,000 to RM590,000 for this unit type, and it is offered for rent at about RM3,000 a month; Sean thinks a let of about RM2,800 to RM2,900 justifies the price. Neighbours he met had no complaints about the developer.

standout.title: A back gate into the park
standout.body: A floor at car-park level holds a kindergarten and a gourmet kitchen, and opens through a gate directly into the master plan's central park, where Sean watched families walking their children. The landscaping runs so seamlessly that you can hardly tell where the development ends and the park begins.

pros: The location, which he knows from studying at TAR College: a new road straight to Jalan Semarak and KLCC, a planned MRT3 line, and an urban park that makes it feel nothing like its surroundings.
The developer's placemaking: a temporary commercial hub that fills a real gap, a park, and Sky Awani affordable blocks designed with such pride that they set the tone for the whole master plan.

The architecture: better roads and landscaping on arrival, a decorated car park, an open-air lobby, 1.9 m corridors, his favourite side-by-side living layout and a facility deck that flows into the park, unbeatable at this price.
cons: The perimeter: narrow village roads and PPR flats with cars parked along the roadside give a poor first impression before you reach the master plan.
Competition: Setapak and Genting Klang have many cheaper projects, though he thinks Edgewood's premium is worth it.

The immediate setting will change: landed village housing and empty plots behind, and even the temporary commercial area, will eventually be developed, so the view isn't guaranteed beyond about ten years.

closing: A standout home at its price, close to the city, for buyers who look past the surrounding streets; Sean says he loves it.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit after completion; prices and rents are from listings as he quoted them. The Makeover Guys, where Sean works, furnished the unit, and he studied at TAR College nearby.
